title: Sen. Jackson introduces legislation outlining 9th District local act framework in North Carolina Senate
text:
State Sen. Brent Jackson has introduced a bill designed to provide a structure for handling matters particular to the 9th Senatorial District, as detailed by the North Carolina State Senate .
Filed as SB 1078 on May 5 in the 2025 regular session, the measure is officially titled: ‘9th Senatorial District Local Act-2.’
Below is our analysis based on the official bill text ; some explanation is included to clarify its content.
The core purpose of the bill is to specify that its guidelines pertain solely to the 9th Senatorial District in North Carolina. It does not put new programs, rules or funding into effect. Rather, it establishes a local act framework intended for district-specific concerns. The legislation will be in force upon becoming law.
During the 2025 regular session, Jackson also filed 17 other legislative proposals.
To become law in North Carolina, bills must go through a multi-step legislative process . Legislators begin by submitting a bill , which is then referred to a committee for evaluation. Each chamber reads the bill three times. If either the House or Senate amends a bill after the other has passed it, both must approve the identical version. Once both bodies pass the same text, it advances to the governor, who has 10 days (or 30 days if the legislature is not in session) to sign, veto, or allow it to become law without a signature.
More information about this bill and other legislative actions can be found here .
Jackson, a Republican, was elected to the North Carolina State Senate in 2023 and now represents the 9th Senate district, succeeding former senator Michael Lee.
